channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] UK: Village votes to 'secede' in asylum center plan protest
item.description: Residents of Piddington, a tiny, remote village in Oxfordshire in England, have staged a "referendum" on leaving the UK. They are objecting to plans to open an asylum reception center at a disused military base nearby.

item.title: [DW] Can Canada and the EU deepen ties to counter Trump?
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is known for standing up to US President Donald Trump. Now he wants to forge a "unique alliance" with Europe. But what could such a partnership look like?

item.title: [DW] Shock in Kosovo as Hague convicts former President Thaci
item.description: The conviction in The Hague of former President Hashim Thaci and three former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has caused consternation in Kosovo — both among political leaders and on the streets. DW reports from Pristina.

item.title: [DW] British-American writer Bonnie Greer dies aged 77
item.description: Chicago-born playwright Bonnie Greer, who became a familiar face in British political discourse later in life, has died. Her husband David Hutchins announced news of Greer's death.

item.title: [DW] Poland reaffirms support for Ukraine after drone strikes
item.description: After Russia's recent drone attacks on targets close to the Ukraine-Poland border, Warsaw has doubled down on its support for Kyiv and pledged a "nonprovocative but serious response" to Moscow.

item.title: [DW] Kosovo ex-president Thaci sentenced to 25 years for war crimes
item.description: A Hague tribunal ruled that Hashim Thaci, a former leader of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA), is responsible for war crimes carried out during the war of independence with Serbia.

item.title: [DW] Turkey's rights groups, EU call out LGBTQ+ crackdown
item.description: Several raids and arrests of LGBTQ+ persons in Turkey have triggered sharp criticism from numerous Turkish organizations — and also from Brussels.

item.title: [DW] Why do authoritarian regimes target the LGBTQ+ community?
item.description: A recent crackdown on the LGBTQ+ community in Turkey is symptomatic of a wider rights regression, according to experts. It's worse under authoritarian regimes, but why is it such a popular policy for these states?

item.title: [DW] Russian birth tourism to Brazil increases
item.description: Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and stricter regulations in Argentina, more and more Russians are choosing to travel to Brazil to give birth to children, who will obtain Brazilian nationality.

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe is trying to ‘replicate’ Silicon Valley. Is it China that offers the better lesson?
item.description: The EU wants Europe's future in European hands, but its flagship scale-up fund leaves the investment strategy to private equity, while China's more targeted venture capital system may offer some better lessons.

item.title: [DW] A war-fatigued and anxious Russia picks a new parliament
item.description: Fuel shortages, drone strikes and mobilization rumors are fueling anxiety and war fatigue in Russia. As support for peace talks grows among Russians, the Kremlin is watching closely ahead of parliamentary elections.

item.title: [EU Observer] Civil partnership from abroad not enough to stay in EU country, according to ECJ preliminary opinion
item.description: As Romania does not recognise same-sex partnerships, having a partner there is not a basis for residency, according to a European Court of Justice opinion on Thursday.

item.title: [EU Observer] Israel triples size of key West Bank settlement, testing von der Leyen’s ‘unacceptable’ rebuke
item.description: The revelation of the West Bank expansion plan came the same day European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen condemned the original, smaller scheme in her State of the Union speech in Strasbourg.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU plans Europe‑wide social media age limits, but can Brussels really police Big Tech?
item.description: A revolution in tech, or another Brussels-bred measure that will fall flat on enforcement? Such has been the debate surrounding the EU's new social media ban for teens, though it is still pending review by law-making bodies.

item.title: [EU Observer] Details emerge on Canada’s ‘associate membership’ EU offer, as Brexit UK left looking on
item.description: EUobserver understands that Ursula von der Leyen did not consult EU governments before making the offer to Canada and there is anxiety in some EU capitals that cosying up to Mark Carney could inflame Donald Trump into re-starting his tariff war with Europe.

item.title: [EU Observer] Russians trying to capture Dobropillia, before the leaves fall from the trees (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,666)
item.description: By concentrating three combined-arms armies and key drone units near Dobropillia, Moscow is gambling on a southern encirclement route that could threaten the Kramatorsk–Sloviansk stronghold without launching a frontal assault.

item.title: [DW] Serbian President Vucic criticizes Kosovo war crimes verdict
item.description: The conviction of four former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has drawn sharply different reactions across the Balkans. Serbia has accused the court of failing to fully address crimes against Serbs.

item.title: [EU Observer] Orbán re-emerges after long summer holiday, as Magyar strips homophobia from child protection laws (Day 128 of the Tisza government)
item.description: Prime minister Péter Magyar tackles the child protection law, moving to strip the Orban-era conflation of homosexuality with paedophilia from Hungary’s laws.

item.title: [DW] King Charles, Earl Spencer clash over Diana death once again
item.description: Buckingham Palace has rejected criticism of King Charles III in a new book by the brother of his late wife, Princess Diana. Earl Charles Spencer has been a fierce critic of his former brother-in-law for decades.

item.title: [Financial Times] Donald Trump bans CNN, MS Now and Politico from White House
item.description: The move is the US president’s latest attempt to crack down on major media outlets in retaliation for their reporting

item.title: [Financial Times] Ex-Apollo executive admits to improperly using company documents
item.description: Imran Siddiqui had been sued by buyout group’s Athene unit over his rival start-up

item.title: [DW] Airport malaria in Germany remains infrequent
item.description: An outbreak of malaria at Frankfurt Airport this summer has raised alarm. Experts believe parasites probably arrived in a passenger's luggage. But with the onset of fall, the risks of contracting the disease are low.

item.title: [Politico Europe] ‘There are no decent parties left’: Sham elections underscore Putin’s grip on Russia
item.description: After a clampdown on anti-war candidates, the choices for Russian voters are even more limited than usual in this weekend's parliamentary elections.

item.title: [Politico Europe] European leaders prepare public for ‘intensified threat’ from Putin
item.description: However, NATO sees no risk of "imminent attack" despite the fresh warnings from countries such as Poland, Lithuania, France and the Netherlands.

item.title: [Financial Times] Yen sinks after BoJ raises rates to highest level since 1995
item.description: Authorities warn of further potential currency intervention after central bank move fails to buoy currency

item.title: [Financial Times] Warren Buffett’s son to succeed his father as Berkshire Hathaway chair
item.description: Conglomerate says the elder Buffett will take on role of chair emeritus

item.title: [Financial Times] Anthropic and the golden rules of business
item.description: Shifts in technology and geopolitics mean the ideal of the perfect company is changing

item.title: [Politico Europe] Australia following Canada as EU associate member is ‘pure speculation,’ says Commission
item.description: Any discussions about other countries would come after "putting flesh on the bone" with Canada.

item.title: [Politico Europe] California’s Newsom signs executive order to explore new AI rules, consider ‘kill switch’
item.description: The move by the California governor comes amid national concerns about the potential existential dangers of the technology.

item.title: [DW] Ever more Israelis moving to and investing in Cyprus
item.description: Over the past three years, more and more Israelis have been purchasing property and investing in Cyprus, with many moving to the island permanently. How has this changed the Cypriot economy and how are locals responding?

item.title: [Politico Europe] Germany gets its first F-35 as Europe’s fighter plans fall apart
item.description: Deliveries are starting for Germany's new F-35 fighter jets, but the debate continues in Berlin about future capabilities.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Macron to call emergency G7 meeting as energy prices spike and Russian hybrid attacks mount
item.description: The French leader warned there was no quick fix to high energy prices, and wars in the Middle East and Ukraine.

item.title: [EU Observer] France in ‘game of chicken’ with EU on Russia sanctions, as clock ticks to expiry deadline
item.description: The talks will resume on Monday, but the EU-27 agreed there would be no more deadline extensions. "It's turned into a game of chicken [with France]," an EU diplomat said.

item.title: [DW] Canada and EU: A look at the bloc's special relationships
item.description: Though Canada may be some distance from Europe geographically, closer political ties are in the cards. With talk of an associate membership, DW takes a look at other arrangements the EU has with particular countries.

item.title: [EU Observer] Beijing tells EU to weaken ‘Made in Europe’ industrial bill ahead of October showdown
item.description: Beijing and Brussels have made demands and counter-demands as talks on their myriad trade disputes hot up. But they could be derailed by a US-China summit in Washington next week.

item.title: [Financial Times] Former Wells Fargo asset manager Allspring explores $4bn sale
item.description: Deal by private equity owners would follow a string of transactions that have reshaped the industry

item.title: [EU Observer] Polish leader Tusk exposes classified figures on sky-high Ukrainian casualties (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,667)
item.description: With tens of thousands of Ukrainians reportedly killed or wounded each month, the coming autumn and winter campaign could stretch Ukraine’s manpower, air defences, and battered cities to breaking point.

item.title: [Financial Times] Swiss sports brand On signs Kylian Mbappé in blow to Nike
item.description: Group targets long-term partnership with French star, similar to relationship with tennis great Roger Federer

item.title: [Politico Europe] Ukraine’s NATO envoy calls for more air defense donations
item.description: Aid to Kyiv is “not a donation but a swap,” said Ukraine’s NATO Ambassador Alyona Getmanchuk.

item.title: [EU Observer] Scene set for verbal punch-up at UN in New York, as Trump and Netanyahu face critics from EU and further afield
item.description: Brazilian leader Lula da Silva will give the opening speech at the UN in New York on Tuesday morning, in which he will "personally" warn Donald Trump not to interfere in Brazilian elections, before Trump takes the floor.

item.title: [Financial Times] Xi’s edge over Trump on AI
item.description: The US president’s anti-regulatory stance fails to take into account that China is catching up

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU to ban metal scrap exports to India, Egypt on environmental grounds
item.description: The two countries are the second and third biggest importers of EU scrap metal.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU commits €3.3bn to Ukrainian drones as funding gap remains unresolved ahead of ‘tough winter’
item.description: As von der Leyen rushes through billions in new funding for Ukrainian drones, EU diplomats are privately questioning Kyiv’s spiralling deficit, while Belgium continues to block the use of frozen Russian assets — intensifying pressure on Europe to find a way to plug Ukraine’s widening funding gap.

item.title: [Politico Europe] British MPs to tackle UK crisis — why it does so badly in Eurovision
item.description: A parliamentary committee will look at the country’s ”dismal“ record in the Eurovision Song Contest.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Far-right Zemmour lets slip French presidential bid
item.description: The controversial pundit is running for president for the second time.

item.title: [EU Observer] Berlin election shows how the EU turns its most mobile citizens into second‑class voters
item.description: European law gives EU citizens the right to vote in municipal elections, but this does not extend to state or national elections, for which Germany reserves voting rights to German citizens. This results in an odd discrepancy even within a single member state.

item.title: [EU Observer] Sweden begins shipping off prisoners to rented Estonian cells
item.description: While Estonia has prison cells to spare, Sweden's prisons are full. Stockholm will pay €30.6m annually for the first 300 prisoners it sends to a Tartu prison. The deal has been criticised by both countries.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: How does the EU plan to ban social media for under-15s?
item.description: The EU Kids Act promises to wean children off endless scrolling and late‑night gaming, but privacy advocates and parts of the tech industry warn the EU’s own age‑verification system could open the door to new risks.

item.title: [Financial Times] Medical AI has a proof problem
item.description: The technology’s advances have not yet translated into big improvements in real-life care
